limitations: This verifies captured ordinary Chrome and readonly owner evidence; no alternative browser driver.

Initial backup FAILED/CLEAN is retained. One unexpired app session and the recovery source refusal rule were observed; attribution to that rule is an inference because the driver reported only generic RECOVERY_DRIVER_FAILED. Successful retry followed ordinary same-instance restart and browser logout without source/data/security changes.

An unused task-created blank tab and stale disconnected Chrome binding were reconciled through documented browser inventory; user tabs remained untouched. Early async snapshots/three mismatched waits were retargeted from current DOM, no duplicate build/start or policy bypass.

Root owned move script initially failed its Split-Path parameter set before any movement, then used native Path.GetDirectoryName and Move-Item with contained absolute targets. Original stopped data was held and byte checked; no data deleted.
Browser tenant change proves immediate old-record clearance; completed empty-list/authorization semantics are independently covered by actual owner focused tests.
Local trusted developer profile only; native phone/provider/hosted/production remains unqualified.
